title: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH)

references.label: Standard clinical hematology laboratory textbooks/manuals (e.g. Henry's Clinical Diagnosis and Management)

explanation: MCH expresses the average mass of hemoglobin contained in a single red blood cell. It tends to track alongside MCV in most anemias (a smaller cell usually also carries less hemoglobin), so MCH is generally interpreted together with MCV and MCHC rather than as an independent classifier on its own.

workedExample.scenario: A hemoglobin of 15 g/dL and an RBC count of 5.0 million/µL.

commonMistakes: Interpreting MCH in isolation as if it were a standalone diagnostic value — it is part of the RBC indices set and is interpreted alongside MCV and MCHC.
